## Problem 1

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(nzelect)
```
### a.Generate a table (which can just be a nicely printed tibble) of vote count (regardless of party) per year/type. Make sure to sort it by vote count.

```{r}
nzge %>%
  group_by(voting_type, election_year) %>%
  summarize(votes = sum(votes)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(votes))
```
### b. Focus only on the 2014 election. Report the proportion of votes for each party in the Candidate election. Again, produce a nice table and sort it by percent of vote.

```{r}
nzge %>%
  
  # keep only candidate votes from the 2014 election
  filter(election_year == 2014 & voting_type == "Candidate") %>%
  
  # total number of votes for each party
  group_by(party) %>%
  summarize(votes = sum(votes)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  arrange(desc(votes)) %>%
  
  # each party's proportion of the total Candidate vote
  mutate(total = sum(votes),
         prop = round(votes/total*100, 3)) %>%
  
  select(-total, -votes)
```

### c.Produce a nice table indicating, for each year, which party won the Candidate vote and which party won the Party vote.

```{r}
nzge %>%
  group_by(voting_type, election_year, party) %>%
  summarize(votes = sum(votes)) %>%
  
  # find the party with the highest vote count in each election
  arrange(election_year, voting_type, desc(votes)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(-votes) %>%
  
  # reshape the results Candidate and Party appear in separate columns
  pivot_wider(names_from = voting_type,
              values_from = party)
```

## Problem 2-Tidyverse: Tennis

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

tennis <- read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/farhadGithub/tennis-atp-data/main/data/raw/atp_matches_2019.csv"
)
```
### a. How many tournaments took place in 2019?

```{r}
tournaments <- tennis %>%
  group_by(tourney_name) %>%
  summarize() %>%
  ungroup()
tournaments %>%
  nrow()

# check the data
tournaments %>%
  filter(str_detect(tourney_name, "Davis Cup")) %>%
  slice(1:5)

tournaments <- tournaments %>%
  mutate(tourney_name = str_replace(tourney_name, "Davis.*", "Davis Cup")) %>%
  group_by(tourney_name) %>%
  summarize() %>%
  ungroup()
tournaments %>%
  nrow()
```
There are only 69 unique tournaments.

## b.Did any player win more than one tournament? If so, how many players won more than one tournament, and how many tournaments did the most winning player(s) win?

```{r}
winners <- tennis %>%
  arrange(tourney_name, desc(match_num)) %>%
  group_by(tourney_name) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(winner_name) %>%
  group_by(winner_name) %>%
  summarize(wins = n()) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(wins)) %>%
  # identify players who won more than one tournament
  filter(wins > 1)
winners %>%
  nrow()

winners %>%
  slice(1:2)
```
There are 17 players who won multiple tournaments. And Rafael Nadal won the most, 9 tournaments.

### c. Is there any evidence that winners have more aces than losers? (If you address this with a hypothesis test, do not use base R functionality - continue to remain in the Tidyverse.)

```{r}
library(tidymodels)
tennis %>%
  select(w_ace, l_ace) %>%
  mutate(win_more = w_ace > l_ace) %>%
  prop_test(win_more ~ NULL, p = 0.5)
```
Yes, we have statistical significant evidence that winners perform more aces than losers.
